subject: Private VPC: scope of wipe, residency guarantees, and evidence for customer-controlled storage
messages:
From: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@medisecure.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medisecure.ai
Date: 2026-10-05T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: Clarify: residency + deletion evidence for Private (VPC) deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at MediSecure is very interested in Redwood Private. Before procurement we need clarification on two operational points around customer-controlled storage in a VPC:

1) When we request a full tenant wipe (end-of-contract or handback), what exact artifacts are deleted from Redwood-controlled systems vs. customer-managed volumes in the VPC? We need to understand the scope (snapshots, replication logs, backups, object-store keys).

2) What form of evidence can Redwood provide to attest deletion? For auditors we usually require (a) a timestamped deletion log, (b) a description of the wipe process, and (c) a signed attestation or cryptographic proof if available.

Attached is a short SOC2 summary for context. Can you share a short operational Q&A or runbook we can include in our security review?

Appreciate it — Sara

[Attachment: SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf)]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@medisecure.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: residency + deletion evidence for Private (VPC) deployment

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear questions and the SOC2 summary. Below is a concise Q&A and the high-level runbook for tenant handback/wipe in a Redwood Private VPC deployment. I'll attach the more detailed playbook and evidence checklist.

Quick answers up front:
- Scope: Redwood only stores control-plane metadata (customer id, config, audit links) in the Redwood control plane; all customer data (model checkpoints you deploy, embeddings, user payloads) can be configured to reside in customer-controlled storage inside the VPC (S3-compatible buckets, NFS volumes). For customer-controlled storage we never move or copy data to Redwood-managed object stores unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
- Snapshots/backups: Automated snapshots taken by Redwood agents in the VPC (for accelerated recovery) are stored in customer buckets by default. If a customer enables Redwood-managed backups, those will be listed explicitly in the onboarding contract and are deleted per the same wipe workflow.
- Deletion evidence: We provide (1) deletion operation logs with timestamps and actor IDs, (2) a wipe manifest showing which buckets/objects/paths were deleted, (3) volume/tombstone confirmations from the VM/node agent, and (4) an optional signed attestation from Redwood Security for contract-level requirements. Cryptographic shredding (re-encryption of keys) is available when KMS is managed by Redwood.

High-level tenant handback runbook (summary):
1) Customer requests handback via support + authorized SSO admin.
2) Escrow & validation: We verify identity, contract terms (retention holds), and any legal holds (takes 24–72 hrs).
3) Snapshot freeze: Redwood triggers agent to quiesce processes and take final snapshots (if customer requested). Snapshots are marked with a unique handback id.
4) Delete pass: Agent performs object deletion in customer bucket(s) per manifest. Deleted object keys are recorded in the handback manifest.
5) KV/tombstone purge: In-memory KV caches and local KV stores are purged; tombstone markers are applied to prevent resurrection during replication.
6) Disk/volume wipe (if requested/contracted): Zeroing/secure-delete is executed on ephemeral volumes; for persistent block volumes we can schedule a crypto-erase (key destruction) if the KMS is Redwood-managed.
7) Evidence package: We compile deletion logs, manifests, agent telemetry, and an operator-signed attestation PDF. We can produce a CSV of deleted object keys for audit ingestion.
8) Final confirmation: Customer signs-off; Redwood marks tenant as complete and removes control-plane metadata according to retention SLA.

Notes and caveats:
- If the customer manages KMS and keys never leave the customer, Redwood cannot perform crypto-erase; we disable access and provide logs for customer to perform key destruction.
- Cross-region replication: If objects replicating to a different region exist, those are handled according to replication rules—either included in the delete manifest or left to the customer if replication is external.

I'm attaching the detailed playbook and evidence checklist (CSV) for your security and procurement teams. If you'd like, Marissa can propose an assisted-wipe dry run (staging) to validate the manifests and evidence flow.

Thanks,
Kimberly

[Attachment: vpc-assisted-wipe-playbook.docx]
[Attachment: evidence-checklist.csv]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T14:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: residency + deletion evidence for Private (VPC) deployment

Sara — quick operational notes from infra/ops perspective (copied to Karthik for contract language):

- Timeline: once authorized, a standard assisted wipe runs ~4–8 hours for medium tenants (10s of TB) and up to 24–48 hours for larger footprints; we provide a staging dry run window (1–2 hours) that produces the manifest without doing deletions.
- Permissive holds: If legal/forensic holds are active, we pause at step 2 above and provide the hold metadata. Holds must be cleared by your legal team or via mutual agreement.
- Evidence format: we provide: (a) CSV of deleted keys, (b) gzipped JSON of agent telemetry and deletion API responses, (c) operator-signed PDF attestation. If needed we can also include S3 object-level DeleteMarkers in the manifest.
- Proof-of-delete options: for customers that require stronger proof we can: (1) include a time-stamped audit entry pushed to your SIEM via webhook, (2) provide a signed attestation (PGP or Redwood PKI), or (3) run a KMS key-destruction flow when Redwood controls the KMS.

If you'd like to proceed, we can schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your security and infra teams next week and then carve out a staging dry-run.

—Marissa

Sara / team — adding a short note on contract wording so procurement can sign off without blocking the security review. Suggested clauses we've used previously: 

1) Residency and custody: "Customer data processed in a Private VPC deployment shall reside in customer-controlled storage within the customer's cloud tenancy unless explicitly configured to be exported to Redwood-managed storage."
2) Wipe scope: "On termination or handback, Redwood will execute the mutually-agreed handback runbook. Redwood will delete data stored in customer-controlled buckets/volumes according to the handback manifest and supply an evidence package within 7 business days."
3) Evidence and attestation: "Redwood will provide operator logs, a deletion manifest, and a signed attestation that the deletion operations completed successfully. Where Redwood manages KMS keys, Redwood may perform crypto-erase and provide key-destruction certificates."

If you want, I can draft a short addendum and share it as a Docusign-ready PDF. The language above is intentionally narrow so it's clear where Redwood responsibilities end (e.g., customer-managed KMS, external replication).

Karthik

Assuming the 7-business-day SLT, we're ready to move forward with a draft addendum and a 30-minute runbook review next week. Can you propose two slots?

Thanks — Sara
